headline: New York Moves to Break Up Protest-Policing Unit
deck: The announced structure separates counterterrorism from protest responses but describes new teams in prospective terms.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he is disbanding the NYPD unit that responds to protests. [E7] Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said she endorsed the changes. [E8]

Established in 2015, the Strategic Response Group had served both terrorism-response and demonstration-policing roles. [E4] Its counterterrorism functions, including heavy-weapons deployments at critical infrastructure, are to be consolidated in the NYPD's Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau. [E3]

City Hall said its Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division will have neither weapons nor arrest powers, while a 30-officer First Amendment Support Team will focus on communication and de-escalation and the NYPD will establish a Patrol Support Division. [E1] That prospective language confirms an announced restructure, not a reported completed transfer.

For First Amendment activities, the announced reforms prohibit kettling, long guns and tear gas, and restrict pepper spray, acoustic devices and the use of bicycles as weapons. [E2] City Hall said prospective unit officers will be vetted against complaint and Internal Affairs records, without specifying which findings automatically disqualify them. [E5]
Mamdani also endorsed the CURB Act, which would put protest-policing restrictions into law. [E6]

evidence_box.fragment: The CDDD will not have weapons or arrest powers. FAST will consist of 30 uniformed officers trained in communication and de-escalation. The NYPD will also establish a new Patrol Support Division (PSD), a unit within the NYPD's Patrol Services Bureau, with vetted officers who will spend most of their time on patrol-related duties and receive specialized crowd management training to support responses to demonstrations.

evidence_box.fragment: The reforms also establish significant new restrictions on the tactics and weapons all officers can use during First Amendment activities, including a formal prohibition on kettling, long guns and tear gas. Pepper spray will not be used as a crowd-management tool, and long-range acoustic devices will be limited to 90 decibels. Officers will also be prohibited from using bicycles as weapons except when necessary to prevent death or physical injury to themselves or another person.

Its deployment at protests, particularly during the 2020 demonstrations following the police killing of George Floyd, drew allegations of excessive force from civil rights groups and prompted calls for the unit to be dissolved.
